title: Americans Use AI to Choose Healthy Snacks, Says Report
paragraphs: Looking for a snack that's high in protein but low in calories? Some Americans are asking AI to help them find one, according to a new report from food company Conagra Brands.

For its Future of Snacking 2026 report, Conagra worked with research company Circana to analyze more than 53 million shopping transactions involving 17,000 snack products. It also looked at what people were asking AI about snacks.

The US snack market is now worth about $198 billion in annual sales, up around 3% from the previous year. Over the past three years, snack sales have grown about 1.4 times faster than food sales overall.
Traditional choices remain popular. Salty snacks such as chips, along with candy and cookies, account for nearly 46% of snack sales.

However, snacks that offer more nutritional value are also doing well. Categories that include protein-rich foods such as yogurt, cottage cheese and dried meat snacks bring in more than $20 billion a year. Dried meat snacks, including products such as Conagra's Slim Jim, account for $5.7 billion, with sales up 9.5% from a year earlier.

The report also found that people are asking AI specific questions about snacks, such as "What is the best low-calorie protein snack?" Conagra says these questions show how nutrition is influencing people's choices, and how AI may be affecting which products they discover.

But people aren't just going online for snack advice. Online shopping now accounts for 13% of snack sales, up two percentage points from a year earlier. The average online snack purchase is also worth 64% more than one made in a store.
For some shoppers, finding a snack may now involve more typing than walking!
